# Environment

Reading, setting and removing environment variables.

<h2 id="environment-variable"><code>EnvironmentVariable</code></h2>

```rux
pub struct EnvironmentVariable {
    pub name: OsStringView;
    pub value: OsStringView;
}
```

One environment variable: its name and its value.
`Copy`. Both views borrow storage the process owns for its whole life.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Process/Src/Environment.rux#L23)

**Fields**

| Name    | Type           | Description                                                                               |
| ------- | -------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`  | `OsStringView` | The name, the units before the first `=`.                                                 |
| `value` | `OsStringView` | The value, every unit after the first `=`, which may itself contain `=` and may be empty. |

<h2 id="environment-iterator"><code>EnvironmentIterator</code></h2>

```rux
pub struct EnvironmentIterator {
    // private fields
}
```

A walk over the environment variables: those the process started with, in the order the system holds them, then
those set since.
`Copy`, holding only a position, so it allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Process/Src/Environment.rux#L97)

<h2 id="variable"><code>Variable</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Variable(name: char8[..]) -> OsStringView?
```

The value of the environment variable `name`, or none when it is not set.
`name` is UTF-8 text. It is matched exactly on the Unix systems and without regard to ASCII case on Windows, which
is how each system matches names. A variable set or removed with `SetVariable` or `RemoveVariable` reads as it was
last changed. When the starting environment names a variable twice, the first is the one returned, as the C
library's `getenv` returns it. A variable set to the empty string is present, with an empty value. The view borrows
storage the process owns for its whole life. Runs in time linear in the size of the environment and allocates
nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Process/Src/Environment.rux#L238)

**Parameters**

| Name   | Type        | Description         |
| ------ | ----------- | ------------------- |
| `name` | `char8[..]` | the variable's name |

**Returns**: the variable's value, or none when no variable has that name

<h2 id="set-variable"><code>SetVariable</code></h2>

```rux
pub func SetVariable(
    name: char8[..],
    value: char8[..]
) -> ! IoError
```

Sets the environment variable `name` to `value`, for this process and every process it starts from now on.
Both are UTF-8 text. The change is seen by [`Variable`](/docs/api/process/environment#variable) and [`Environment`](/docs/api/process/environment#environment), by [`Command`](/docs/api/process/command#command), and on Windows by the system;
the C library's own environment on the Unix systems is not changed. Views handed out before stay valid.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Process/Src/Environment.rux#L349)

**Parameters**

| Name    | Type        | Description                                                       |
| ------- | ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`  | `char8[..]` | the variable's name, which may not be empty or contain `=` or NUL |
| `value` | `char8[..]` | its new value, which may not contain NUL                          |

**Returns**: nothing, or fails with `InvalidInput` for a name or value the environment cannot hold

<h2 id="remove-variable"><code>RemoveVariable</code></h2>

```rux
pub func RemoveVariable(name: char8[..]) -> ! IoError
```

Removes the environment variable `name`, for this process and every process it starts from now on.
Removing a variable that is not set does nothing. Views of its value handed out before stay valid.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Process/Src/Environment.rux#L364)

**Parameters**

| Name   | Type        | Description                                                       |
| ------ | ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name` | `char8[..]` | the variable's name, which may not be empty or contain `=` or NUL |

**Returns**: nothing, or fails with `InvalidInput` for a name the environment cannot hold
